pathSubtitle: Run and participate in meetings — from setting the agenda to handling disagreements and closing with action points.

lessons.title: Starting a Meeting
lessons.situation: You are the team leader starting a weekly update meeting.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: OK, let's get started. Thanks everyone for coming. Today's agenda has three points: project update, budget review, and next steps.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague A
dialogue.text: Before we begin, can we add one item? We got feedback from the client this morning.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Of course. We'll add that as point four. Right — project update first. Where are we?

dialogue.speaker: Colleague B
dialogue.text: We're on track. Phase one is complete and phase two starts next Monday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Any blockers?

dialogue.speaker: Colleague B
dialogue.text: One small one — we're waiting on sign-off from legal. Should be done by Friday.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: OK. Let's move on to the budget.

words.definition: a list of items to discuss at a meeting
words.example: The agenda for today has five points.

words.definition: progressing as planned
words.example: The project is on track for the October deadline.

words.definition: a problem that stops progress
words.example: We have one blocker — approval from management.

words.definition: official approval for something
words.example: We need sign-off before we can proceed.

words.definition: to go to the next topic or item
words.example: Let's move on to the next agenda point.

lessons.title: Presenting Data
lessons.situation: You are presenting quarterly sales data to your manager and team.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll take you through the Q3 numbers. As you can see on the slide, total revenue was up 12% compared to Q2.

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: That's encouraging. What's driving that growth?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Two main factors. First, the new product line launched in August — it performed above expectations. Second, we expanded into the German market, which contributed around 4% of total revenue.

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: And what about the North America numbers? They look flat.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, North America is a concern. We saw a slowdown in July and August. We believe it's seasonal, but we're monitoring it closely.

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: Good. What's the forecast for Q4?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We're projecting 15–18% growth, assuming the new campaign lands well in October.

words.definition: income from business activity
words.example: Revenue increased by 10% this quarter.

words.definition: doing better than predicted
words.example: The new product is performing above expectations.

words.definition: not growing or declining; staying the same
words.example: Sales were flat in the third quarter.

words.definition: changing regularly with the season
words.example: The slowdown is likely seasonal.

words.definition: predicting or forecasting a future amount
words.example: We are projecting a 20% increase.

lessons.title: Disagreeing Professionally
lessons.situation: During a strategy meeting, you respectfully disagree with a proposal.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: I think we should move to a fully remote model. It's cheaper and employees seem to prefer it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I take your point on cost, and I agree remote flexibility matters. However, I'd push back on making it fully remote. We've seen a real drop in cross-team collaboration since we shifted last year.

dialogue.speaker: Colleague
dialogue.text: That could be a training issue rather than a structural one.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Possibly. But the data from our last engagement survey suggests it's more than that — satisfaction in junior staff dropped 15 points, and they specifically cited isolation.

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: Both fair points. Could we explore a hybrid model as a middle ground?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's exactly what I'd propose. Two or three anchor days in the office, flexibility for the rest.

words.definition: to express disagreement or resistance to an idea
words.example: I need to push back on that suggestion.

words.definition: working together with others
words.example: Good collaboration is key to project success.

words.definition: a questionnaire measuring how committed and motivated employees feel
words.example: The engagement survey results were concerning.

words.definition: a system combining remote and in-office work
words.example: We moved to a hybrid model after the pandemic.

words.definition: a fixed day that all employees come into the office
words.example: Wednesday is our anchor day for team meetings.

lessons.title: Closing & Action Points
lessons.situation: You are wrapping up a meeting and assigning clear next steps.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: OK, I think we've covered everything. Let me summarise what we've agreed before we close.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: David, you're going to finalize the budget proposal by Wednesday. Maria, you'll follow up with the client about their feedback. And I'll set up the legal sign-off call for Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: Quick question — for the budget, should I include the contingency line or keep it separate?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Include it but label it clearly. Let's keep everything in one document.

dialogue.speaker: Maria
dialogue.text: And for the client follow-up — email or call?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Try the call first. If you can't reach them by Tuesday afternoon, send an email.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Minutes will go out by end of day. Thanks everyone — productive session.

words.definition: to give the main points briefly
words.example: Let me summarise what we discussed.

words.definition: a specific task someone must complete after a meeting
words.example: You have three action points from today's meeting.

words.definition: a reserve budget for unexpected costs
words.example: We always include a 10% contingency in project budgets.

words.definition: the official written record of what was said in a meeting
words.example: Can you send the meeting minutes by Thursday?

words.definition: achieving a lot; effective
words.example: That was a very productive conversation.

lessons.title: High-Stakes Executive Meeting
lessons.situation: You are presenting a major strategic recommendation to the executive board.

dialogue.speaker: CEO
dialogue.text: You've had three months to review the acquisition target. What's your recommendation?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Our recommendation is to proceed, subject to the resolution of two outstanding due diligence concerns — their IP ownership structure and the pending litigation in the German subsidiary.

dialogue.speaker: CFO
dialogue.text: Walk me through your valuation rationale.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We used a DCF model with a WACC of 8.5% and a terminal growth rate of 2.5%, which gives a base-case valuation of $420 million. We stress-tested against a downside scenario where revenue growth is 30% below projection and still saw positive NPV.

dialogue.speaker: CEO
dialogue.text: What's your confidence level on the IP issue being resolved before close?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Moderate. Their legal team is engaged and we have a fallback clause in the term sheet that protects our position if it isn't resolved within 60 days.

dialogue.speaker: CEO
dialogue.text: Good. We'll put this to a vote next week once the full board has reviewed the deck.

words.definition: a thorough investigation before completing a business deal
words.example: We completed due diligence before signing the contract.

words.definition: the process of taking legal action
words.example: The company is involved in ongoing litigation.

words.definition: an estimate of how much something is worth
words.example: The startup's valuation was $500 million.

words.definition: evaluated under extreme or unfavourable conditions
words.example: We stress-tested the model against a recession scenario.

words.definition: a provision in an agreement that protects a party if something goes wrong
words.example: The contract has a fallback clause in case of delays.
